title: Hydraulic Power — Green System Engine Driven Pump — Case Drain Architecture Retrofit
abstract: Retrofit of the redesigned pump case with a scavenge gallery, a hard-faced shaft seal and a case drain flow sensor, deleting the repeat drive pad cavity check imposed by the earlier interim kit.

sections.planning_reason: The interim seal kit reduced fluid migration into the accessory gearbox drive pad but did not remove it, and it left the fleet carrying a repeat cavity check every 1200 flight hours. The check needs the fan cowl open, so it is frequently deferred, and three aircraft reached the reservoir refill line between checks. The original case has no scavenge path, so any leakage past the primary seal has nowhere to go except the drive pad. Only a case change closes it.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin installs the redesigned pump, whose case carries a scavenge gallery returning primary seal leakage to the case drain and whose shaft has a hard-faced ceramic running surface against a carbon primary seal. A case drain flow sensor is added and the pressure transmitter is relocated to the new gallery boss so that a rising case drain flow is annunciated before the reservoir level falls.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fan cowl and get access to the pump from zone 123. Depressurise the green system and drain the pump case. Remove the pump and the existing case drain line. Install the redesigned pump with the re-ported valve D2910110251872 and torque the mounting flange with the longer grip barrel nuts EN529286-2D. Install the case drain flow sensor GRDE393470-41 and route its harness to the connector in zone 193. Relocate the transmitter D2910110594226 to the gallery boss and connect it. Refill and bleed the green system. Do the pump operational test and confirm that the case drain flow indication reads within the band given in the accomplishment instructions. Re-secure the clamp of FIN 280GG8 and close the fan cowl. Delete the repeat drive pad cavity check from the aircraft maintenance programme and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all classic model ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft not yet at the case drain architecture standard, including aircraft carrying the withdrawn interim seal kit. Aircraft delivered after the production cut-in already have the redesigned pump. Embodiment supersedes the interim kit and its repeat cavity check.
sections.material_note: Kit K2910-1067-01 contains the redesigned pump, the flow sensor, the harness and the barrel nut set for one engine position. Two kits are required per aircraft. Lead time is twenty-four weeks and the pump is the long-lead item. Removed pumps are returned to Aeralis for overhaul credit.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next engine driven pump change, or within 36 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
